title: Deterministic alias-sync failure: triage + cross-deployment hotfix and customer escalation path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During an automated model alias promotion the model-catalog alias rewrite introduced a deterministic mismatch between alias metadata and live model binary IDs. The serving runtime uses the model alias + model-id to namespace KV cache entries. The alias rewrite left a subset of frontends (Hosted) referencing a different namespace shape than Dedicated/Private nodes, producing deterministic generation regressions and an uptick in safety filter hits for several tenants. Several customer escalations came in between 2026-03-01 02:10 UTC and 2026-03-01 05:30 UTC. This ticket coordinates triage, an immediate cross-deployment mitigation, and a staged hotfix + postmortem and customer comms plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Promote model alias 'prod' -> 'prod-v2' with alias-rewrite job that updates model catalog metadata
2) Send identical prompt to Hosted endpoint (alias resolves via new metadata) and Dedicated endpoint (local routing cached old model-id namespace),
3) Observe deterministic token divergence starting at token 1 in generation and mismatched KV cache keys in logs (kv.namespace shows different suffix),
4) Reproduce reliably by replaying canary slice traffic via synthetic harness with original request IDs.
mitigation_steps: Immediate: Pause automatic alias promotions (flip flag in control-plane) and pin affected tenants to model-specific model-id.

Short-term: Invalidate KV cache namespaces for Hosted nodes by issuing 'kv:flush-namespace <alias-v2>' to force recompute of keys, coordinated with Dedicated ops to avoid simultaneous full-cache flush.
Customer-facing: Open personalized incident threads for top 5 impacted tenants and provide rollback to prod-v1 with traffic split 100% while patch is validated.
proposed_solution: Root cause: alias rewrite injected a new 'alias_revision' token into catalog metadata but the runtime namespace versioning only handled 'model_id' and 'model_hash'. The fix requires (1) catalog writer defensive migration to emit backward-compatible namespace_shape, (2) runtime tolerant lookup that falls back to previous namespace patterns for 24h after alias change, and (3) an audit job to reconcile mixed namespaces. Implementation plan: runtime patch (PR runtime#12984) adds fallback lookup and logs deprecation warnings; catalog patch (PR catalog#2046) lands a migration path. Both patches gated behind an integration test that replays canary traffic.
rollout_plan: 1) Validate runtime fallback patch in staging with synthetic canary harness (hours: 3),
2) Deploy to Hosted control-plane nodes with 10% traffic for 30m, monitor divergence metrics,
3) If stable, promote to 50% for 1h, then 100% for Hosted,
4) Coordinate Dedicated/Private node upgrades during a maintenance window to sync catalog writer changes; for Dedicated, use rolling upgrade with tenant-aware drains,
5) Close customer rollbacks and transition tenants back to alias flow after 48h of stable metrics.
